scores.claim_text: Ask Sage (acquired Dec 31, 2025 for $271.6M) is used by 16,000 government teams, 100,000 DoW users, 2,500 companies; FedRAMP + IL5/IL6/TS.
scores.supports: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts(Ask Sage) returned 43 DoD contract awards totaling $23.07M, all Department of Defense — including ASK SAGE Army Decentralized IDIQ, Air Force SBIR/STTR, NSWC, Center for Army Analysis, Army Test and Evaluation Command, ASA(ALT), DASA DES, and 318th RANS task orders.
scores.interpretation: Heavy DoD adoption of Ask Sage at task-order level corroborates the deployment-at-scale claim. The exact 100,000 DoW users figure isn't directly verifiable, but task-order pattern across many Army/Air Force/Navy components is consistent with broad rollout. PASS. Acquisition price ($271.6M) vs trailing DoD subscription revenue (~$23M cumulative) is a valuation question, not a claim-falsification one.

scores.claim_text: ConductorOS was 'central to' Talisman Sabre 2025; multi-national joint exercise.

No counterparty filing mentions ConductorOS/Talisman Sabre integration with BBAI. scores.claim_text: FY2025 revenue $127.7M; US gov 90% ($114.7M); 10%+-concentration customers = $65M (51% of revenue).
scores.supports: Direct USAspending lookup of BigBear.ai Federal LLC returned only 8 awards totaling $15.3M lifetime ($7M EXIM-Bank, $8.3M DoD). Direct DoD-prime contracts are far below the $114.7M FY25 US government revenue claim, implying the vast majority is earned as SUBCONTRACTOR work to prime integrators — typical pattern for cleared mid-cap defense services. Acquired entities ProModel ($35M lifetime, 30 awards) and NuWave ($12M lifetime, 8 awards) account for additional direct prime revenue. Revenue DECLINED 19.3% YoY ($158.2M -> $127.7M) despite narrative of 'strongest financial position in history.' Air Force EPASS wound down. Single-customer A/R of $3.4M >10% (new concentration in FY25, not present in FY24).
scores.M_value: BigBear.ai Federal LLC: 8 awards, $15.3M lifetime; ProModel: 30 awards $35M; NuWave: 8 awards $12M
scores.interpretation: US government revenue claim is plausible only with heavy subcontract intermediation. Year-over-year revenue decline of ~20%, combined with single-customer A/R >10% concentration and material $65M=51% revenue concentration in 10%+ customers, plus EPASS wind-down — supports MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the upbeat narrative. Not a hard contradiction (subcontract pattern is real), but the marketing-vs-reality gap is material.

scores.claim_text: $248M total backlog at 12/31/25; $27M attributable to 10%+-customers; only $8.2M of Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO).
scores.supports: The 30x gap between '$248M total backlog' (non-GAAP, includes Unfunded Backlog + Priced Unexercised Options + Unpriced Unexercised Options per BBAI's own definitions) and the ASC 606 GAAP RPO of $8.2M is extreme. Only $8.2M is contractually firm (signed sales orders); the remainder depends on funding appropriations, option exercises, and unpriced option execution. Even within the $248M, only $27M is from the customers driving 51% of revenue and expected to recognize within 2026. Risk-factor language explicitly warns: 'the contracts comprising our backlog may not result in actual revenue in any particular period or at all.'
scores.M_check: filing-internal cross-check (RPO $8.2M vs backlog $248M); usaspending verification of prime relationships
scores.M_value: Total backlog $248M vs ASC 606 RPO $8.2M (~30x gap)
scores.interpretation: Backlog disclosure conflates ceiling/option value with firm contract value. This is the defense-services analog of Calibration Heuristic 9 (pilot-vs-deployment conflation): unfunded/optioned backlog presented as commercial visibility. The $8.2M RPO is the only number bound by GAAP. SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY of the backlog narrative — headline overstates near-term contracted revenue by an order of magnitude.

scores.claim_text: BigBear.ai holds patent IP across AI, computer vision, predictive analytics, biometrics, perception, orchestration and digital identity.
scores.supports: uspto_odp.query_assignee returned 0 granted patents for 'BigBear', 0 for 'Pangiam' (the recently-acquired biometrics/digital-identity subsidiary that was the IP cornerstone of the digital-identity narrative), 0 for 'ProModel', 0 for 'Ask Sage', and 0 for 'Open Solutions'. The one acquired entity with material patents is NuWave (44 granted), and Analex (2 granted, may not be BBAI's Analex). The biometrics/computer-vision/orchestration tech areas the 10-K markets most heavily have no granted-patent footprint under USPTO assignee search.
scores.M_check: uspto_odp.query_assignee for BigBear / Pangiam / Ask Sage / subs
scores.M_value: n_granted: BigBear=0, Pangiam=0, Ask Sage=0, ProModel=0, NuWave=44
scores.interpretation: Filing language is careful ('not dependent on any particular patent or application'), which is consistent with the absence of a BBAI-branded patent footprint. The biometrics-and-digital-identity narrative (acquired via Pangiam for biometric/digital-identity tech) is not supported by Pangiam having granted patents under that name. Calibration Heuristic 8 applies in reverse: BBAI sells SERVICES + software, not patentable hardware. The patent claim is soft to begin with, but the marketed 'forefront of technological advancement' framing of biometrics/digital-identity vs zero Pangiam-branded patents = MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the tech-leadership narrative.

scores.claim_text: $461.5M total liquidity at 12/31/25; debt reduced from $200.8M to $17.7M subsequent to year-end (88% reduction). 'Strongest financial position in history.'
scores.supports: Cross-check is filing-internal (no external M-source needed for the dollar figures themselves). The $461.5M liquidity number is real BUT was achieved by selling 142,253,313 shares under three ATM agreements in FY2025 alone for $637M gross. Common stock outstanding ballooned from 251,554,378 (12/31/24) to 436,955,655 (12/31/25), a 73.7% one-year share-count increase. Debt reduction was achieved primarily by CONVERSION of 2029 Convertible Notes into common stock (38.1M shares issued in Jan 2026), not by cash repayment. Combined dilution YoY is well over 90% when including the convert-driven shares. Restructuring charges of $4.37M in FY25 (vs $1.29M in FY24) indicate ongoing organizational disruption.
scores.M_check: filing-internal: share count, ATM proceeds, convert mechanics, restructuring activity
scores.M_value: shares: 251.5M -> 436.9M (+73.7%); ATM gross $637M FY25; 2029 notes converted to 38.1M shares Jan 2026; restructuring $4.37M FY25
scores.interpretation: Liquidity is real but bought at extreme dilution + convert-into-equity rather than retire-with-cash. Calibration Heuristic 10 applies (distress fingerprints): three back-to-back ATMs in one year, mass convert-to-equity, growing restructuring charges. The 'strongest in history' framing of capital structure ignores that capital-raising came from share issuance, not cash generation. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY of the balance-sheet-strength narrative.

scores.claim_text: Pangiam acquisition (Feb 2024) brought biometric/digital identity capabilities; Air Force EPASS wound down Q2 2023; cost of revenues rose to 78% in FY25 (vs 71% in FY24).
scores.supports: usaspending recipient='Pangiam' returned 0 federal awards 2020-2026 — the biometric/digital-identity acquisition has no detectable direct federal contract revenue under its own name. Cost of revenues at 78% of revenue (FY25) leaves only ~22% gross margin, far below typical defense-software multiples. Air Force EPASS wind-down (Q2 2023) was confirmed as a material revenue drag in FY24 vs FY23, and that drag has not been offset by new program wins large enough to keep total revenue flat (FY25 is down 19% YoY).
scores.M_value: Pangiam direct awards=0; cost of rev: FY25=78%, FY24=71%, FY23=74%
scores.interpretation: Pangiam's biometrics capability does not appear as a federal-prime revenue line. Either it is also subcontracted (typical for cleared biometrics work to CBP/TSA via primes) or commercial in nature. Combined with margin compression and EPASS wind-down, the 'transformation' narrative is moderate-underdelivery. MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY.
